fences: a surrendered battle's outcomes write exactly once, through the ordinary defeat-ending outcome path — a surrender-specific outcome channel is a landing defect
mercy deeds sit under #269's existing good-deed daily credit cap (+4/day) — the cap is the farm fence
honours read battle facts, not ending types; a mercy shown to the same Ranger twice in a day is counted once
one offer per Ranger per battle (a refused offer may not be re-offered) — no surrender loops
antiFarming.rule: #70's anti-exploit discipline + #177's no-double-count shape, applied to an ending

note: Surrender is a persons' system: it exists because both sides can speak (#301) and be held to account (#269). Zero offers exist; the two deed rows land as proposals into #269's file (STAGING step 2).

offer.command: a battle command class of its own, proposed into #10's ring vocabulary for Ranger battles only
offer.npcSide: an #18 AI decision keyed to #93/#301 character facts — some Rangers never offer, and never-offering is character data, never a generic die roll
offer.timing: on the offerer's turn, in place of another command; may be offered at any point by choice, not only at collapse — early surrender may be wisdom, cowardice, or bluff

stakes.fence: #210's law entire: field-duel stakes are honours only — never Mochi, never currency, never Fragments — and surrender changes the ending, never the stakes
stakes.noTransfer: a surrender may never be a vehicle for transferring a Mochi ('I yield, take my partner' is inexpressible — keepers change by #38/#168/#217/#268, the closed list)

mercyAccept.deed: mercy shown — small positive row, PROPOSED into #269's table
mercyAccept.effect: the battle ends on the offer; the stakes settle as a fought-out ending does; witnessed mercy feeds #270's tallies as witnessed good

mercyRefused.deed: mercy refused — small negative row, PROPOSED into #269's table
mercyRefused.effect: the battle continues to defeat-only endings; the offer may not be re-offered this battle

postTheft.rule: a surrender offered after a steal landed in the same battle (#356) routes the winner to restitution's bigger choice (#275: return on the spot is the strongest deed, not the mercy's small one) — the surrender system does not soften theft

wildExclusion: wild battles have no surrender — a wild Mochi offers no terms; the wild ending grammar is flight (#254), and a closed-heart wild individual's ending is #349/#288's road, never a negotiation
